original_question: For semigroup elements a and b, define a ∼p b when there exist u and v in the semigroup with a = uv and b = vu. If a semigroup has the property that ∼p is transitive in every variant of that semigroup, where the variant at an element c has multiplication x ◦ y = xcy, must ∼p already be transitive in the original semigroup?
target_in_paper: The draft targets the paper’s treatment of Problem 6.22 from Araújo–Kinyon–Konieczny–Malheiro, as restated in Section 1 and again at the start of Section 5: whether transitivity of ~_p in all variants of a semigroup forces transitivity of ~_p in the semigroup itself. In this paper, that problem is answered negatively by Example 5.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant relation as primary conjugacy ~_p, correctly focuses on its transitivity, correctly uses the notion of a variant with multiplication x ◦ y = xcy, and correctly asks the converse implication that is the precise open problem discussed in the paper.
missing_details: The question should fix one semigroup S and quantify all variables explicitly: a,b in S, and c in S for the variants.
It should state that the variant is the semigroup S_c=(S,◦_c) on the same underlying set S, with x ◦_c y = xcy for all x,y in S.

To be fully stand-alone, it should specify the exact convention used for primary conjugacy. In the standard formulation behind this problem, a ~_p b means there exist u,v in S^1 such that a=uv and b=vu, where S^1 is S with an identity adjoined if necessary.
It should make explicit that the problem is about arbitrary semigroups; no finiteness, regularity, embeddability, or identity assumptions are imposed.
It should phrase transitivity as a property of the binary relation ~_p on each variant S_c and on S itself.
refined_question: Let S be a semigroup, and define primary conjugacy on S by a ~_p b if there exist u,v in S^1 such that a=uv and b=vu, where S^1 denotes S with an identity adjoined if necessary. For each c in S, let S_c=(S,◦_c) be the variant of S at c, defined by x ◦_c y = xcy for all x,y in S. If the relation ~_p is transitive on every variant S_c, must ~_p already be transitive on S?
justification: Section 1 explicitly identifies Problem 6.22 as asking whether ~_p must be transitive in a semigroup whenever it is transitive in all of its variants, and Section 5 restates exactly that question before giving a counterexample in Example 5.3. So your draft is aimed at the correct narrow target, but it needs the full quantifier structure and the exact stand-alone formulation of the relation and of the variants.
